note: One entry shape, checked by both languages (I03).
The TypeScript client and the Go server each decide for themselves what a
well-formed entry is, and for a long time they decided differently: the
server refused an empty authenticator on a file and accepted one on a
folder (F20), while the client checked neither and two other things the
server also checks. Nothing compared the two lists, so a divergence was
only ever found by meeting one in a vault.
Every case here is fed to store.Entry.Validate in Go and to
checkEntryShape in TypeScript, and both have to reach the same verdict.
A case that is valid must be accepted by both; a case that is not must be
refused by both. Adding a rule to one side without the other fails here,
which is the whole point of the file.
The client is the side that matters most for the invalid cases. A server
is not obliged to be honest, so every shape the server refuses to store is
a shape a hostile one can still send, and the client has to refuse it on
the way in rather than trust that it was never written.
`ceilings` is the second thing both sides write down separately (R26). The
client caps what a handshake may raise its own memory limits to, and it has
to have those numbers in hand before the handshake, so it cannot read them
off the wire. Two copies of a constant drift, and this one drifts into a
client that kills a connection over a batch the server was entitled to send.

note: Name-derived strings and wire numbers both implementations assert they hold.
prefix || base64url(body || crc32), unpadded and canonical (unused bits zero).
body = version (1 byte, 1) || token (16 bytes) || len(url) (1 byte) || url (UTF-8)
|| len(vault) (1 byte) || vault (UTF-8).
crc32 is IEEE CRC-32 over body, big-endian. Nothing may follow the vault.
url is canonical: ws:// or wss://, printable ASCII only, no trailing slash.
vault is a name: 1 to 64 bytes, no control characters.
Decoders trim ASCII space, tab, CR and LF at both ends, and nothing else; every other character
must be in the base64url alphabet (Go's decoder skips CR and LF inside the input, so check first).
Every bad vector must be refused. Why is for people; the wording of refusals is each side's own.

bad.why: unused bits that are not zero
a flipped bit, so the CRC fails
a url with a trailing slash
a vault name with a control character
a length that runs past the end
a newline inside, which Go's base64 decoder would silently skip
a non-breaking space before it, which is not trimmed

note: frame = marker (1 byte) || payload. marker 0: payload is the raw chunk. marker 1: raw DEFLATE (RFC 1951).
A receiver refuses a frame longer than chunkMax + 1 bytes before inflating anything,
refuses a payload that inflates past chunkMax, refuses a chunk of zero bytes,
then hashes the raw bytes and compares them with the name it asked for.
Bytes after the final deflate block are ignored: they cannot change the decoded bytes, which the name checks.
A sender uses marker 1 only when the deflated payload is shorter than the raw bytes.
Deflate output need not match between implementations; decoded bytes and names must.

note: fold(s) = NFC(table applied code point by code point to NFC(s)).
The table is Unicode full case folding (CaseFolding.txt statuses C and F) at unicodeVersion.
Each implementation carries a generated copy and must prove its digest equals tableDigest:
SHA-256 over lines 'XXXX:YYYY ZZZZ\n', uppercase hex, at least four digits, sorted by source code point.
Neither runtime's own lower-casing is the specification; Go and JavaScript disagree on U+0130.
Each case is UTF-8 bytes in hex, because JSON cannot carry invalid UTF-8 and Go's decoder
replaces lone surrogates. reason is the first rule broken, in the order plan/protocol.md lists them,
and both implementations must report the same reason, not just refuse.

note: Five policies, kept separate even where two agree today (PLAN M0.5 task 3).
syncable: the path rules above. chunkingText: an extension in textExtensions, compared in ASCII lower case;
it only picks chunk sizes, so a wrong answer costs efficiency, never correctness.
searchable and mcpReadable: syncable, and ending .md or .txt in any ASCII case, drawings included.
mcpEditable: mcpReadable and not ending .excalidraw.md in any ASCII case.
Windows only, applied by the client to inbound paths (PLAN section 4.12); the server does not.
reason: character (one of <>:"|?* in a segment), trailing (a segment ends with a dot or space),
reserved (a segment whose part before its first dot, trailing spaces removed, is a reserved device
name in ASCII case-insensitive comparison), checked per segment in that order. null: writable.
